newsitem.title: UK: Frank Field to take welfare reform post in UK govt.
newsitem.headline: Frank Field to take welfare reform post in UK govt.

text.p: Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair has appointed Frank Field, a leading thinker and campaigner on welfare reform, to the post of minister of state for social security, Downing Street sources said on Saturday.
The junior ministerial post will put Field, a specialist in the area of pensions, in charge of long-term planning for welfare reform.
"He knows his field and Tony has immense respect for his ability," said one senior Downing Street aide. "This is an area which requires very bold thinking."

Pensions were a key battleground in the election campaign, during which Labour accused the outgoing Conservatives of planning to abolish the state pension and replace it with a privately funded system.
Field has argued for a two-tier system that would maintain the basic state pension while expanding second-tier, funded pensions for the majority of the population.
The announcement was unusual in that it came before some cabinet-rank ministerial appointments had been confirmed.
